policy_name: Production Incident Severity and Escalation Policy

SEV-1.name: Critical Incident
conditions: Primary database filesystem storage utilization >= 90% with positive growth rate (> 500MB/min).
Imminent risk of PostgreSQL PANIC due to inability to write to pg_wal/ directory.
Total connection saturation: active sessions at max_connections and application receives FATAL connection errors.
Catastrophic primary crash, hardware failure, or unrecoverable split-brain scenario.
Transaction ID wraparound failure threshold approached (< 1,000,000 transactions until forced shutdown).
operational_impact: Complete user-facing outage or transaction processing halted.
Data write operations blocked across all production services.
Severe business revenue and customer SLA breach.
evidence_required: Filesystem metrics showing storage >= 90% or pg_wal/ size exceeding retention limits.
pg_replication_slots query output demonstrating multi-gigabyte restart_lsn lag or dead slot.
pg_stat_activity output showing connection count equal to max_connections or superuser-only access.
Exact error log traces containing 'PANIC: could not write to file pg_wal' or 'FATAL: remaining connection slots'.
escalation_conditions: Incident not contained within 15 minutes of alert trigger.
Cause remains unknown or ambiguous after initial triage.
Root cause requires destructive action (dropping replication slots, terminating active client sessions).

human_approval_requirements.approval_protocol: Explicit two-person authorization recorded in incident channel prior to executing destructive commands (e.g., pg_drop_replication_slot, manual failover).

SEV-2.name: High Severity Incident
conditions: Standby replica replication lag exceeds SLO (> 100MB or > 60 seconds duration).
Primary filesystem utilization between 75% and 89% with steady growth.
Connection count >= 80% of max_connections, or elevated PgBouncer client wait queues.
Lock contention wave or deadlock frequency exceeding 10 per minute.
Autovacuum unable to keep pace, causing noticeable table/index bloat on core tables.
operational_impact: Read replicas serving stale data to customer-facing APIs.
P95 / P99 latency spikes causing degraded user experience.
Risk of escalation to SEV-1 if left unmitigated.
evidence_required: pg_stat_activity query output with connection breakdown by state and top wait events.
pg_locks and pg_blocking_pids output identifying blocking transactions.
pg_stat_archiver metrics demonstrating failed WAL archive attempts.
escalation_conditions: Standby lag continues to grow after 30 minutes of standard troubleshooting.
Blocking PID belongs to a critical background batch job or migration.
Underlying cause is ambiguous or documentation retrieval yields insufficient evidence.

human_approval_requirements.approval_protocol: DBA approval required before terminating blocking backend PIDs or modifying configuration parameters (e.g., max_standby_streaming_delay).

SEV-3.name: Medium Severity Incident
conditions: Isolated slow query regressions impacting non-critical services.
Temporary disk consumption spike (65% - 74%) during large batch reports.
Autovacuum freeze warnings with > 20,000,000 transactions before wraparound limit.
Minor connection pool spikes that resolve autonomously within 5 minutes.
operational_impact: Localized latency degradation on specific internal endpoints.
evidence_required: Autovacuum execution logs and relation tuple age metrics.
Storage trend graphs over a 24-hour baseline.
escalation_conditions: Condition persists for > 4 hours without resolution.
Trend analysis projects degradation into SEV-2 within 12 hours.

human_approval_requirements.approval_protocol: Standard engineering review and scheduled deployment window.

SEV-4.name: Low Severity / Advisory
conditions: Informational alert or minor configuration drift.
Non-blocking log warnings (e.g. temporary client disconnection, checkpoint starting).
Sub-optimal index suggestions or routine maintenance scheduling.
evidence_required: PostgreSQL log extracts or configuration diffs.

human_approval_requirements.approval_protocol: Standard Git pull request or Jira ticket.

ambiguous_incident_policy.description: Whenever an alert payload or on-call observation lacks sufficient authoritative evidence, ambiguous symptoms are detected, or retrieval confidence falls below 0.70, the system MUST NOT formulate speculative hypotheses or suggest unverified remediations.

human_approval_guardrail.description: All destructive, terminating, dropping, rebooting, or failover actions require verified human sign-off. The assistant operates strictly in an advisory capacity.
